g.title: all-role-information
g.text: All-role illustrative request/response interfaces | not an institutional protocol

a.xlink:title: C01\nOrdering / treating physician
C06\nRegistered nurse providing \ndirect care
A direct-care RN, payer UM nurse and nurse case manager are different functions even if one person can hold more than one role.
C08\nMedical assistant / \nclinical-support assistant
Specific clinical tasks depend on state rules and training; this role is not interchangeable with a physician assistant.
G01\nProvider medical director / \nchief medical officer
Actual reporting lines, medical-staff authority and privileges require local bylaws/organization chart; no universal CMO-boss graph is asserted.
M17\nRespiratory therapist
Specific protocols and privileges determine independent adjustments; state and setting must be checked.
M18\nDischarge planner / \ntransitions coordinator
Hospital 482.43 permits development by or under RN, social worker or other qualified personnel; do not impose RN-only staffing nationally.
M25\nEquipment supplier / delivery \nor fitting staff
The CMS power-mobility example has specific requirements; do not apply those mechanically to all equipment.
M26\nInfusion / other \nreceiving-service coordinator
Operational service-coordination model; exact service procedure and clinical signoffs require the actual provider protocol.
M27\nPalliative-care clinical team \nmember
A team function comprising different professions, each retaining its own scope; identify the actual clinician for an order.
O01\nProvider authorization / \nprecertification specialist
Works for requester; not payer intake. Local payer requirements and request stage determine the needed packet.

O13
External diagnostic / 
clinical evidence author or 
custodian
This is an evidence-supply function spanning distinct professions, not a claim that laboratory staff, radiologists and therapists have identical permissions.
P01\nPatient / insured member
Capacity, minors, emergencies and surrogate authority require applicable law and case facts; this is not a blanket consent rule.
License, privileges and clinical setting control the activity; this is not a hierarchy over insurer employees.
P03\nLegally recognized personal \nrepresentative
No universal national ordering of spouses, adult children or guardians is asserted; resolve governing state law and actual appointment.

P05
Healthcare interpreter / 
communication-access 
professional
Qualification and access arrangements must fit the communication need; interpreting is distinct from written translation.
C02\nReferring / primary-care \nclinician
C03\nTreating / performing \nspecialist
Clinical responsibility must be assigned for the actual service; specialist is not necessarily the organizational supervisor of the PCP.
M01\nLead care manager / case \nmanager

Credential may be nursing, social work or another background; separate coordination authority from that credential. Published staffing examples differ; this is not evidence of national role prevalence.
O02\nReferral coordinator
May share a job with scheduling or authorization; preserve those functions as separate milestones.
May be a physician, NP or PA under the relevant professional rules; this is a functional role, not an additional credential.
Clinical responsibility must be assigned for the actual service; specialist is not necessarily the organizational supervisor of the PCP.
C04\nNurse practitioner

Specify state, population focus, privileges and any required practice arrangement before concluding independent authority. California examples separate practice category, furnishing authority and employer requirements. Prospective 104-availability wording is not proof of present individual certification or application availability.

C05
Physician assistant / 
associate 
(jurisdiction-specific title)
PA means physician assistant in this profile; prior authorization is written out to avoid acronym confusion.
A direct-care RN, payer UM nurse and nurse case manager are different functions even if one person can hold more than one role.
C07\nLicensed practical / \nvocational nurse
State law and setting determine supervision and permitted activities; staffing title alone is insufficient.

M28
Hospice interdisciplinary 
group and attending functions 
(distinct roles)

V11, V16 and V17 are the official October 2025 codification, not a complete current-2026 update check. They distinguish IDG/designated RN coordination, physician certification and admission. A patient-designated attending may have a different allowed credential; that does not grant every attending terminal-illness certification authority.
State law and setting determine supervision and permitted activities; staffing title alone is insufficient.

G03\nUM / medical-policy committee \nand specialty members
G08\nPolicy analyst / clinical \nregulatory adviser

G04\nCare-management director / \nmanager
G06\nQuality-improvement / audit \nprofessional

G07\nTrainer / clinical educator
A clinical educator may hold a clinical license, but its separate practice permissions are not supplied by the training title.
G09\nCompliance / regulatory \nprofessional
Actual legal interpretation and enforcement authority depend on role; local compliance staff are not the regulator.

population-health data 
analyst

G12\nBusiness / workflow analyst
Systems analyst authority is change-process authority, not authority over patient treatment.
Partnership documents several management levels; exact titles and reporting relationships elsewhere remain local.

application-support 
professional

O07\nMedical coding specialist

Standing, filing and any amount-in-controversy rules must be checked; no threshold amounts are invented here.
J02\nMedicare Appeals Council \nreviewer
The precise review scope and procedural requirements require the actual notice/rules; no automatic appeal entitlement is implied.

M02
Medical social worker 
(credential-dependent 
practice)

Job titles and licensure differ; distinguish supportive casework from licensed clinical treatment. UCLA describes a pre-licensure Clinical Social Worker II assignment; clinical job wording does not establish independent clinical licensure.
M03\nLicensed clinical social \nworker
Exact clinical activities and independent practice depend on state license and setting, not a national generic job description.
M04\nClinical / community \npharmacist

Professional scope, collaborative arrangements and specific state permissions must be identified for therapy changes. Washington CDTA is one documented pathway for specified therapy activity; no universal requirement for a new physician instruction on each authorized action is inferred.
M06\nTreating psychiatrist
Treating psychiatrist and coverage reviewer must be identified separately even where both are physicians.
M07\nClinical psychologist

Prescribing and specialty testing permissions are jurisdiction- and qualification-specific. New Mexico documents additional conditional/full prescribing certification; ordinary psychology licensure alone does not establish it.
M08\nLicensed behavioral-health / \nsubstance-use counselor
Mental-health, addiction, marriage/family and peer credentials have different requirements; establish the specific credential before assigning clinical authority.
M09\nCommunity health worker
Community trust does not substitute for clinical licensure; program training and role determine permitted services.
M10\nPatient navigator
May be a nurse, social worker, CHW or other trained worker; apply the actual credentials in addition to navigation role.
M11\nHealth-care guide / \nnonclinical care guide
Partnership HealthPlan documents this title as an organizational example; do not impose it on every care program.

M12
Registered dietitian / 
qualified nutrition 
professional
Credential, state rules, referral/order and facility privileges determine specific clinical permissions.
M13\nHealth educator / \nself-management coach
A licensed clinician may also provide education; distinguish the educational function from any separate clinical authority.
M14\nPhysical therapist

State/direct-access, order and payer requirements can differ; do not infer one universal physician-supervision hierarchy. No particular state direct-access rule was established in this audit; attempted V20 was unavailable and is not used as proof.
M15\nOccupational therapist
Order, setting and scope requirements must be identified for the actual service.
M16\nSpeech-language pathologist
Language access and speech/swallowing impairment are different needs and may require different professionals.
M23\nTransportation coordinator / \ndispatcher
Functional synthesis from access-barrier and transport-support evidence; exact broker rules and payment route are not established here.

M30
Administrative care 
coordinator / scheduling 
support
Administrative coordinator and licensed case manager may be distinct posts; do not infer credentials from title.
P02\nInformal caregiver / family \nsupport person
Information sharing depends on permitted involvement; access is not automatically access to the entire record.

Job titles and licensure differ; distinguish supportive casework from licensed clinical treatment. UCLA describes a pre-licensure Clinical Social Worker II assignment; clinical job wording does not establish independent clinical licensure.

Safeguarding / 
protection-service 
professional

U02\nPayer eligibility / benefit \nspecialist

Exact benefit authority and decision notice are plan-specific; not every benefits specialist is authorized to issue a denial. R13 permits some assigned benefit-only decisions; actual signatory authority still requires the plan/delegation.
U03\nPayer nurse / licensed UM \nclinical reviewer

Under MA 422.566(d), anticipated adverse medical necessity requires appropriate licensed professional review; local policy may impose stricter physician escalation. R13 has both a wider professional-category list and medical-director final-responsibility language. Specific case review/signoff must be clarified, not inferred from either statement alone.
U06\nPayer behavioral-health \nreviewer

Psychiatrist, psychologist and counselor credentials are not interchangeable; apply actual product and review requirements. Medication pathways can differ from medical-service prior authorization and Part C item/service appeals. R13 has both a wider professional-category list and medical-director final-responsibility language. Specific case review/signoff must be clarified, not inferred from either statement alone.
